analysis.causality: Separate measured component changes from hypotheses about bandwidth, compute efficiency and CPU/kernel-launch overhead. CUDA event intervals include device idle time between launches; profiler overhead excluded from primary timing
analysis.decision: Do not automatically launch the full epoch or increase budget. Report measured speed/cost tradeoff, warm-window stability, remaining input reconstruction and budget needs.
analysis.projection: Steady-state train-loop time/cost only; data reconstruction, future validation/checkpointing, cold-start compilation and interruptions additional

budget.rule: Full CPU input verification before either GPU. Refresh live spend before each stage; reserve CPU plus both GPU attempts. No retries or new hardware arms without a new bounded plan.

design.legacy_commit_handling: Verify every frozen training dependency byte against the original training commit, preserve that legacy resume-contract commit and record the actual orchestration commit separately; no resume-check bypass
design.outputs: Metrics and profiles only; no model/checkpoint writes, no validation/arena or W&B runs
design.parity: Same model/optimizer/data/RNG contract; BF16 kernels can differ by GPU. Report first-step loss/gradient norms and later trajectory drift; no claim of bitwise cross-hardware training equivalence
design.primary: Elapsed wall time difference from end-update 510 to end-update 550 / 40; cost per update at declared GPU+CPU+RAM resource rates
design.recipe: Unmodified HH-002 Hero recipe, parameter BF16, eager BT4, compiled fresh regions, original rematerialization and optimizer
design.secondary: Four fixed ten-update blocks, input wait, transfer, forward/backward/optimizer CUDA event intervals, peak memory, GPU telemetry, one separate instrumented CPU/CUDA trace

protocol.question: Does H100 reduce HH-002 epoch training time and cost relative to L40S, and which workload components limit scaling?
